_note: In-season video/TikTok takes injected by the fantasy-video-inject skill. Note-only, ALWAYS week-tagged: nothing here casts a vote in the board's value math. Notes older than TTL weeks stop being shown/injected.

jacory croskey-merritt.note: Concern: Washington's Tunsil tricep injury drags down the whole offense's red-zone trips, and the backfield split (White getting receiving work, little RB-target history under Jayden Daniels) means Croskey-Merritt's goal-line share alone may not be enough for weekly startable upside.

Second opinion, more bullish than Smyth's: BDGE loves the value if healthy — showed real efficiency last year behind a banged-up line with a backup QB, and it's easier for an early-down back to catch dump-offs than for Rashod White to take early-down work. Caveat: an undisclosed lower-body injury as of late August, and Jayden Daniels has a very low RB target share.

jeremiyah love.note: Rostered by team 9, not a waiver target. Opens the season in a muddled committee (Braswell/Beck) so casual managers will undervalue him, but FSC expects his workload to ramp toward 17-18 PPG by the back half. Their call: buy-low trade around week 5 for roughly 4th-round redraft value.

Fine taking him mid-to-late third. He probably won't be the goal-line back and the injury nearly guarantees a slow start, but the PPR receiving volume is there and the preseason usage was strong (8 of 11 snaps, seven straight to open the game). Smyth's comp is Jahmyr Gibbs as a round-three rookie, not a first-round rookie price.

FSE is not drafting him: rookie who missed the camp reps he needs, ~10% reinjury rate, recovery runs right up against Week 1, and Tyler Allgeier likely opens as the starter. His plan is to let someone else own him and trade for him around Week 4.

chase brown.note: 8 red-zone targets in 8 games with Burrow, and similar in 2024 — a real, repeated receiving role in the red zone, not a one-year blip. Smyth prices an RB red-zone target at 4.4x a normal carry, same as a goal-line carry.

Third option in the receiving game with no backfield competition added (Sorsdahl-type only plays 3rd-and-long, ~24% of snaps). Cincinnati may be the NFL's highest-scoring offense; even a small run-heavy tilt inside the 5 could back him into the rushing TD lead.
FSE's single safest round-2 player and ranked 10th overall on his board: no backfield competition, elite offense and QB, and a real receiving role (4.1 rec / 5.2 targets per game, 88 targets).

kyren williams.note: 3rd among RBs in red-zone routes — the passing-game red-zone role is priced into his floor, so a bad rushing TD split hurts him less than it looks.

christian mccaffrey.note: Far and away the leader in RB red-zone targets — the single biggest edge in the metric.

Camp absences are rest, not injury — no high ankle, MCL or hamstring. The predictable part is workload: 100+ targets, all the goal-line work, most early downs. Efficiency (3.9-4.0 YPC) doesn't matter at that volume.
Maybe the riskiest player in fantasy — 30 years old, long injury history, and a decimated 49ers roster — but healthy he was the best fantasy RB last year and in 2023. Not currently hurt.

javonte williams.note: Red-zone-target leader but Smyth expects some decline from that rate; still projects a good share. Buy the role, not last year's exact number.

Higher on him recently — the Dallas RB2 competition has collapsed (the talk about limiting his workload has gone quiet; the backups are behind Malik Davis). Expect roughly a repeat of last year minus some goal-line luck, on a top-five offense.
Boring but real: Dallas should score a huge number of points with Pickens and Lamb healthy in year two. Jaydon Blue takes passing work, not early downs. BDGE projects 12-15 rushing TDs.
Clean projection as long as he stays the best RB on Dallas — always in the red zone. Only risk is talent: Jaydon Blue or Malik Davis playing well could eat touches.

kenny gainwell.note: Red-zone target usage is a good sign for the Pittsburgh backfield duo — Gainwell's pass-game role gives him standalone value even in a split.

jaylen warren.note: Other half of the Pittsburgh duo Smyth flags as a positive on RB red-zone targets.

Pittsburgh backfield is a floor play, not a ceiling play — volume is split but total volume is high in the Rodgers offense, and each back is a strong handcuff for the other. Smyth prefers Warren in full PPR, less so half.

kenneth walker iii.note: Riser: Kareem Hunt's red-zone target volume from last season vacates into Walker's role.
Foot scare — missed practice. Encouraging signs: no brace, no support, walking normally, so Smyth reads it as a precautionary camp rest for a star back rather than a real injury.

Foot scare doesn't look serious. KC paid him to be the workhorse with no real backfield competition, and camp buzz is heavy screen usage early. Mahomes back from the ACL means they lean on him. Goal-line TD upside inside the 5.

The whole risk is talent: if he is not a three-down bell cow for Kansas City they lean on Emmett Johnson, Brashard Smith in two-minute and a third-down back. Offense insulates him, play style makes him boom/bust.

chuba hubbard.note: Riser: had the red-zone-target role last season and lands back in the same situation.

Carolina will NOT stay 50/50 for long — Canales historically picks one back and rides him. Precedent: Dowdle was the RB2 in fantasy for five weeks, Hubbard came back and it went 80/20 Hubbard immediately. Whoever wins it is an easy top-20 RB; both carry injury risk.

cam skattebo.note: Riser: 4 red-zone targets in only 6 games as a rookie — the ability showed up in a small sample.

Odds of a bell-cow role have gone up in the past two weeks — Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary as the RB2 competition is a great sign. Expect the team to ramp him slowly, but the volume signals all point the right way.
Coming off a tibia fracture, ankle dislocation and ruptured deltoid ligament — efficiency was already thin at 4.1 yards per carry, and the Giants signing Najee Harris is a warning sign.

james cook iii.note: Watch item: only 3 red-zone targets last year, but persistent reports the staff wants to throw to RBs more, and Buffalo is in the red zone a lot. Upside is in the change, not the history.

The hidden lever is receiving work: Ty Johnson has been out for weeks with an undisclosed injury. If Cook gets to 50-60 catches on top of 300 carries and goal-line work in an 11-win offense, he's a top-3 RB. Pete Carmichael from the Payton tree dumps off to backs constantly.
The RB version of a clean projection — 26.9 years old, no injury history, no competition for touches, led the NFL at 95.4 rush yds/game, and he wins whether Buffalo runs or passes more.

d'andre swift.note: Negative: 1 red-zone target across the past two seasons, and Chicago ranks 32nd in RB red-zone target share under Caleb Williams — they go pass-heavy in the red zone without involving the back.

Moved UP to his RB21: Monangai's injury covers the first month, and pre-split last season Swift averaged nearly 16 ppg while the offense was still bad. Safe floor pick in a very risky RB range, even though his goal-line and target work are thin.
Safe in the mid rounds: Chicago is a plus touch environment for RBs and his main competition, Kyle Monangai, has a knee hyperextension — so at minimum expect a hot start.

tony pollard.note: Negative: only 1 red-zone target — no receiving role near the goal line, so his TD equity depends entirely on carries.

Even lower. He has finished around RB23 three years running WHILE getting bell-cow volume (only he, Saquon and Henry hit 275+ touches three straight years). At 29, behind this line, with Tyjae Spears set for a bigger role and a likely-bad defense, Smyth doesn't see the turnaround.

jordan mason.note: Negative: only 1 red-zone target — offense goes pass-heavy in the red zone without targeting the RB.

Role change: per The Athletic's Vikings beat, Minnesota is literally restructuring its run scheme around Mason on the San Francisco template. Aaron Jones is old and injury-prone. Committee risk is real but they want Mason to take the job. Cheap RB add.

quinshon judkins.note: Negative: zero red-zone targets (as with Dobbins) — no pass-game red-zone role to fall back on.

Still a red flag. Smyth expects a Derrick Henry usage shape with none of the Henry upside — Dylan Sampson takes the receiving work, the O-line is entirely new with zero snaps together, and a worse defense means fewer positive game scripts.
FSE's contrarian safe pick: as a 22-year-old rookie starter from Weeks 3-15 with no training camp behind the league's worst O-line he was still an RB2 producer. He projects him for 300 touches.

luther burden iii.note: Groin/abductor strain upgraded to a ~1-month absence, which FSC reads as a partial (grade 2) tear given the timeline. 15-25% reinjury rate on return — fading him, not chasing the discount even if his price drops.
Risk worth taking if you like the talent — thin career production and a groin strain, but he is running in practice and the Chicago offense and projected role support an upside swing.

mike evans.note: Grade-1 quad strain on top of 9 lower-body injuries in 7 seasons and a team change; still not practicing a week+ later. ~30% hamstring-family recurrence rate. FSC would pass unless he falls a full round below current ADP.
FSE is taking him off his board entirely: chronic hamstring strains, a current quad injury and an earlier groin issue. He would let a league-mate pay the name price.

malik nabers.note: ACL recovery — avoided the PUP list (better than the 70-80% chance they gave it a month ago) but could still miss 1-3 games to start. ~80-90% odds of returning to pre-injury level, 20-25% reinjury risk over 2 years. Fine as a 3rd-round pick, too risky as a 2nd.
Looking healthy. Smyth is fine taking him at his WR24 slot over a TE like McBride on pure value.

Free at the 2/3 turn. Reports have flipped 180 in the last month — non-contact jersey shed, Harbaugh says Week 1 is reasonable. Wan'Dale Robinson gone. Expect ~90-95% of him for ~90% of the season; a couple rusty early weeks is the whole risk.
Ranked in round 2 on his board but knee-dependent — one tweak from IR. The McCaffrey of WRs: first-round value at a third-round price if healthy.

patrick mahomes.note: Cleared for camp practicing unrestricted, will sit all preseason. Reinjury risk ~20-25% if held back a week or two, jumps to ~40% if he plays week 1 (inside the 9-month post-ACL-surgery threshold). Separately: his rush volume normalizes down and FSC worries about a 'silent killer' QB8-11 season like 2024.

tucker kraft.note: ACL tear from week 8 last year, off the PUP, ~10 months post-op by week 1 — expect ~4 weeks of reduced snaps/efficiency after his return. FSC is passing at his 6th-7th round price: his 2025 breakout games all came with Jayden Reed/Christian Watson/Matthew Golden hurt or ineffective, and that target competition is healthier this year.

Moved UP to TE5 (from TE7) on camp news: full pads, full 11-on-11, heavy target volume — not a limited ramp-up. He has self-reported a snap count for the first month or two, but he survives on ~6 targets a game rather than needing volume, and Musgrave being hurt forces him onto the field.

Mid-round set-and-forget TE. Back from the ACL tear and BDGE isn't worried; Green Bay's room is condensed and should throw more. Expect 8-9 point floors with 18-22 point spikes — better than any TE drafted after him.

george kittle.note: Achilles speed-bridge repair, off the pure PUP-only concern and running routes; return date unclear (6-9 months post-surgery ≈ mid-Oct, but speed-bridge patients have beaten that timeline before). <2% reinjury rate — FSC prefers him over Tucker Kraft as the swing injury-TE bet given the much lower recurrence risk.

bucky irving.note: Shoulder dislocation/surgery, full camp participant and appears fully recovered; 10-20% instability/reinjury risk remains. FSC thinks the market hasn't repriced him despite the good news — backup Kenneth Gainwell profiles as a passing-down/2-minute back, not a real threat to his 65-70% share of TB touches.

Buy-low on volume: Tampa Bay was a top-10 red-zone-volume offense for RBs in 2024 (Irving over 2 combined RZ touches/game before injury cut his 2025 short). New OC should restore that passing-game RZ role; Gainwell/Sean Tucker will chip in but Smyth doesn't expect a repeat of last year's near-zero goal-line share.

Positive signs. Sean Tucker could be cut (a clear plus if so), and even if not, Gainwell looks like a change-of-pace third-down back rather than a real threat — Smyth doesn't expect him to take more than a typical backup's share. More signs Irving sees red-zone work.

tank dell.note: ~20 months post major Dec-2024 knee injury, officially back at camp but not yet cleared for 11-on-11 (only 7-on-7 so far). 50-80% odds of returning to pre-injury level. Price hasn't moved on the good news — FSC likes him as a very late-round dart in deep/best-ball formats, believes he's still Houston's #2 WR if healthy.

zay flowers.note: Quad contusion — minor, expected to miss only a few days of practice. Not a concern.
Safe — first crack at being the No. 1 for a healthy Lamar Jackson, and he already posted a WR13 per-game / WR7 overall season.

devonta smith.note: Hamstring injury, low concern — further along in recovery than the Eagles' rookie WR dealing with the same issue, and has existing chemistry with the QB. FSC expects him healthy for week 1 and is still drafting him at current price.

With A.J. Brown gone he steps into the alpha role, and he's an elite separator who has produced every time Brown was off the field. His outside competition is Danta[v]ion Wicks; the rookie is slot-only. Could compete for the NFL lead in target share. Buy him if the market still prices him as a WR2.
Three top-20 per-game seasons while sharing with A.J. Brown in a low-volume offense. With Brown gone FSE thinks he should cost a round earlier than he does on ESPN/Sleeper.

xavier worthy.note: Shoulder sprain on the same shoulder that had offseason surgery — team says he avoided a major injury, but FSC's concern is elevated because it's a repeat structure that has to hold up all year. Recommends holding off at current ADP until he's back on the field; ~15-25% recurrence rate.

jordan james.note: Fractured a rib July 30, currently not practicing with no official return date; typical recovery 4-6 weeks. Should have time to heal for week 1, but is missing camp reps his fellow backup Keelan Black is getting — FSC expects Black to beat him back and take the early lead for the 49ers' RB2 job behind McCaffrey.

laremy tunsil.note: Tricep tear, likely needs surgery, 4-6 month recovery — could miss most or all of the season, especially if Washington's record is bad enough to shut him down. Losing a top-tier LT off an already below-average line is a real drag on Jayden Daniels/Terry McLaurin/the Washington backfield, independent of any injury to those players themselves.

jonathon brooks.note: ACL recovery, full camp participant with no limitations, beat reporters calling him explosive again. ~60% odds of returning to pre-injury level (skews high given his age). Price has already run up (ADP ~120 to ~88) as the market caught up — FSC still likes him as a 3rd-round pick but the value edge from a month ago is mostly gone.

alec pierce.note: Started camp on the PUP list, still not practicing, no clear return timetable as of this recording (Aug 10-13). Watch for an update before drafting him.
Coming off offseason ankle surgery — may suit up Week 1 but will need roughly a month to ramp. Stash-and-bench, not a Week 1 start; the second-half version is worth about a 5th-round redraft price.

david montgomery.note: Cooling him off around RB20: Woody Marks is getting real work and this is trending toward a genuine split, not an RB2 split. Montgomery is a floor play with bust risk and no upside behind it — and Dan Campbell already cut him from ~50% to ~30% of touches last year.

bhayshul tuten.note: Still the green upside swing but camp has made him more boom/bust — some days he's the offense's best receiving weapon, other days he fumbles and loses goal-line work. LeQuint Allen's injury is a small plus for his pass-protection snaps.
The RB version of the Burden bet: almost no production, but he is the starting back for Liam Coen, whose system produced Bucky Irving in Tampa.

rhamondre stevenson.note: Smyth now ranks him ABOVE TreVeyon Henderson. Camp reporting is consistently 'Stevenson is the early-down back and the pass blocker; Henderson change-of-pace if he can handle pass pro.' You get the starting RB on a top offense in round seven instead of round five.

treveyon henderson.note: Downgraded below Rhamondre Stevenson. Hasn't flashed the traits that drove last year's camp buzz, and the staff is framing him as change-of-pace contingent on pass protection. Top-5 upside is real but Smyth doesn't see a startable role early, which is hard to survive from a round-five pick.

Sliding down FSE's rankings — New England looks like a Josh McDaniels committee, and with a healthy Rhamondre Stevenson it is hard for Henderson to win the job outright. Only a Stevenson injury unlocks the lead role.

rico dowdle.note: Other half of the Carolina split. Smyth sees ceiling here rather than floor — Canales goes all-in on one back, so this is a bet on which one, with Rashaad White / Hubbard / Dowdle as the three-year precedent for the winner paying off big.

josh jacobs.note: Fading him. An 'old 28' with a huge career touch count, a horrid offensive line, a possible suspension, a current injury, and the offense shifting to more three-receiver sets with tight ends hurt. Smyth would rather take Javonte Williams or Kyren Williams for similar production and less risk.

Two misdemeanor charges filed for a May incident, NFL discipline unresolved as of Aug 28. Also 28.5 years old, faded late in each of the last two seasons, injured in two of three, with Marshawn Lloyd rising into a more even split.

rj harvey.note: Warming up slightly. The staff has shown real commitment to him and the offseason noise (Dobbins, Coleman) has gone the other way. His ADP has slid from RB25 to RB31/32 while the news improved — that gap is the reason to take the shot, not the talent.

kyle pitts.note: Not a believer. The QB situation is scary even in the Penix case, and the split is damning: Pitts was not a top-12 TE in games where Drake London was on the field, under either QB.

harold fannin jr..note: Small tick DOWN. His value is easy quick-hitting targets and YAC in a bad offense, and the rookie WR is projected to take some of those short/screen targets away. The offense being bad is priced in; losing the easy-target share is the new part.

sam laporta.note: Small tick DOWN on injury news — people Smyth trusts are cautious about it, and in a range where TE5-TE8 go inside six picks, a minor injury matters a lot. Detroit also has plenty of other options. He'd take him if he falls, not reach.
Drew Petzing takes over as OC — the coordinator who let Trey McBride eat. LaPorta returned to practice after a couple weeks out, so the injury isn't a concern.

Safe now that he is back at practice; the hip issue looks like a one-off bad hit. Detroit has the easiest schedule in football and FSE thinks they will be the best offense in the league, which outweighs sharing targets with St. Brown and Jameson Williams.

ashton jeanty.note: Injury is now being reported as possibly a LOW ankle sprain, not a high ankle sprain — likely limited in Week 1 but little effect on the rest of the season. He has a great Week 1 matchup, which is the annoying part. Smyth still wants him in the second round.

Risky only because of the ankle. Their injury writer reads the low/high uncertainty as a probable grade-2 low ankle sprain, so missed time is live — and a volume-dependent back gets hurt more the more he touches it.

nico collins.note: Big bump — moved above Drake London. Smyth's under-the-radar worry was Jaden Higgins taking targets in a low-volume passing offense, and without Higgins that risk is gone. Boutte's arrival is a PLUS: it moves Collins into the Z role instead of being pressed every snap. He was the overall WR2 in points per game across his 15 healthy games in 2024.

Target share should spike: Jayden Higgins tore his ACL and Tank Dell can't string practices together. Houston traded for Kayshon Boutte, a pure downfield X — if that moves Collins off the X (85% of his routes are outside, never in motion), it's a further boost. Mike Clay projects C.J. Stroud 8th in pass attempts.

FSE moved him up to 17th overall after the Jayden Higgins ACL tear. Kayshon Boutte is a career X receiver (75% of snaps), so Collins should finally get moved around the formation instead of only running big-boy routes into No. 1 corners — a possible career-high 28-30% target share.

chris olave.note: Ranked above Rashee Rice, which does not match ADP. The Jordan Tyson target-hog scenario has not materialized, so the only real worry left is the concussion history — and Smyth is fine paying that price.

rashee rice.note: Yellow flag in full PPR (red-ish in half). The knee is visibly not fully healthy, and the 'he's a YAC guy, separation doesn't matter' defense fails because YAC needs a healthy knee. A new OC likely means far fewer screens (he led the NFL in screens by 2x), and Kenneth Walker takes red-zone touches.
Risky for off-field/suspension reasons, plus a poor training camp and Mahomes coming off an ACL. FSE will take him at ADP but not above it.

dj moore.note: Positive. He looks like the clear focal point in Buffalo under his old Panthers coach. Reference point: he was 6th in WR target share and only finished WR21 — in Buffalo, even 15th in target share should make him a top-15 receiver. Fine at his round-five price over riskier backs.

terry mclaurin.note: Diggs does NOT hurt him as much as the market thinks. Every report has Diggs as the SLOT receiver, not the WR2 — same as New England last year, where he came off the field in two-receiver sets. McLaurin stays the clear number-one target in the new offense.

Risky both ways: 31 years old on a Washington offense that looks to be collapsing (Tunsil out at left tackle, Diggs added), and even in his big 2024 he was only WR16 per game despite 13 receiving TDs.

stefon diggs.note: Reports point to a slot-only role that comes off the field in two-receiver sets. Solid PPR floor play in deeper leagues, but not the WR2 in target volume that people are pricing in.

josh downs.note: ADP has dropped further than Smyth's opinion has — buy the discount. The Colts keep Downs in two-receiver sets and Keenan Allen only comes on for three-WR looks (playing outside, Downs slides to slot). Allen is entering year 14, in decline, and scored ~11-12 ppg last season, so the target hit is small.

Downgrade: new calf injury on top of the Keenan Allen signing, with Alec Pierce and Tyler Warren both expected ready for Week 1. BDGE has not seen Shane Steichen trust Downs as an every-down player. Sell-high window if anyone still prices him as the Colts' slot alpha.

carnell tate.note: Hesitant now. The ADP (WR32 for a top-five NFL draft pick) was the appeal, but his preseason was genuinely bad, and his path needs the Titans offense to be merely below-average rather than horrible. Smyth would rather take Brian Thomas Jr. one spot earlier and buy the Jacksonville offense instead.

denzel boston.note: Dynasty yes, redraft no. He profiles as the outside X receiver, which makes him heavily dependent on QB play and red-zone trips — and this offense is unlikely to give him either.

travis etienne jr..note: Alvin Kamara sprained his MCL and is out at least a month, so ETN has a clean bellcow window over the first ~4 weeks. Saints also get healthy O-linemen back plus David Edwards, run Kellen Moore's uptempo dome offense, and have one of the easiest early schedules. Buy/start him now, not later.

tyler warren.note: Vegas has his season reception line at 74.5 — higher than Tetairoa McMillan, Jaylen Waddle, Luther Burden. Colts are devoid of weapons (Pittman gone, Pierce recovering from ankle surgery, Downs with a calf). Set-and-forget TE1; don't trade him for a shinier name.
Underrated mid-round league winner — Indianapolis has to funnel the offense through him with Alec Pierce coming off injury, Josh Downs' two-WR-set role unclear, and Keenan Allen old.

michael pittman jr..note: Buy-low in PPR: BDGE ranks him OVER DK Metcalf straight up. Pittman fits what Aaron Rodgers is now (six catches a game over the middle) far better than Metcalf, who only works behind the LOS or 40 yards downfield. Kenny Gainwell gone, and the Arthur Smith -> Mike McCarthy switch should raise Pittsburgh's pass rate.

dalton kincaid.note: Highest-upside late TE on the board. Snap share should climb from ~50% to ~65%, and his per-snap / per-target / per-route metrics are already elite among fantasy TEs. PCL injury derailed 2025; healthy now and attached to Josh Allen. A top-4 TE finish would surprise nobody.

christian watson.note: Every-down role in a condensed Green Bay room (no Doubs, no Wicks). Golden plays pure X and Reed plays slot in 11 personnel, so Watson gets moved around for easy separation. Green Bay's O-line is bad at run blocking — Love's preseason snaps were mostly under-center play action, which points to a higher pass rate.

matthew golden.note: Camp reports say full-time player running the X role with a consolidated target share. Worth another chance in 2026 at a late price.

j.k. dobbins.note: Cheap RB2 in a great spot: Denver has the NFL's #1 O-line and Sean Payton's scheme feeds RB receptions. He saw 14+ carries in every game but one last year before the injury, and Denver re-signed him with real money. BDGE thinks R.J. Harvey is explosive but not a good runner.

jakobi meyers.note: Undervalued because he's boring. Jacksonville runs high-volume over-the-middle work under Liam Coen and Trevor Lawrence clearly trusts him and Parker Washington — sure hands, savvy routes, right place at the right time.

parker washington.note: Jacksonville's WR1 through the summer, and the team says he's essentially never coming off the field (11/12/13/21 personnel). All three of Jacksonville's 100-yard receiving games last season were his, all in the final quarter of the year.

emeka egbuka.note: Toe sprain was a 2-3 week timeline that started ~2 weeks ago, so no real Week 1 concern as of filming. Mike Evans is gone and Zac Robinson (the OC who moved Drake London all over the formation in Atlanta) will not ask Egbuka to play X — Tez Johnson and Jalen McMillan do that. Expect fantasy-friendly route volume.

trevor lawrence.note: BDGE's QB6. Liam Coen calling plays, a trusted weapons group (Meyers, Parker Washington, Brenton Strange, BTJ stretching the field, Hunter on 20-30% of snaps), plus 4-6 rushing TDs a year. Cheap streaming-proof QB1.

jayden daniels.note: Round-6 QB with league-winning rushing upside — ~4,500 total yards and 30+ TDs as a rookie with almost 900 rushing yards. The Stefon Diggs signing gives him a real WR2 next to McLaurin.

de'zhaun stribling.note: Deep sleeper WR with a real path: SF's early-2nd rounder, huge camp and preseason buzz. Mike Evans re-aggravated a quad, Ricky Pearsall is out for the year, Jauan Jennings gone — the 49ers barely have receivers. Projects as a power slot for Purdy with Kittle back from the Achilles.

puka nacua.note: BDGE's WR1 even accounting for a possible one-game suspension — he sees the setup as a repeat of Cooper Kupp's 2021.

Elite when on the field (best fantasy WR last year, top-6 all three seasons, contract year) but carries real suspension risk from off-field allegations plus current muscle soreness. FSE guesses a suspension may be pushed back past the Australia opener.

wan'dale robinson.note: Very likely to lead the Titans in targets AND receptions. Brian Daboll came in and immediately gave him $70M, and he ran 140 targets in back-to-back seasons under Daboll in New York. Carnell Tate gets the yards; Robinson gets the PPR volume.

colston loveland.note: Best bet among Bears pass catchers to return value. He averaged 18-20 PPR points per game down the stretch last year, and Ben Johnson's very first move was handpicking him 10th overall.

jahmyr gibbs.note: BDGE's 1.01, ahead of Bijan Robinson — Detroit is letting him be a true bellcow and this could be an all-time RB season. He rates Atlanta's QB situation as a genuine risk to Bijan.

amon-ra st. brown.note: Safest WR in round 1: top-6 in three straight seasons, plays through injuries, and Detroit has the easiest schedule in football with Jameson Williams opening the field.

ceedee lamb.note: Clean, not explosive: top-12 WR four years running with Dak and heavy pass volume, but only 3 and 6 receiving TDs the last two years and George Pickens caps his ceiling.

jonathan taylor.note: FSE fades him: huge career touch count, age 27.5, missed 3/7/6 games in 2024/23/22, and the Colts around him got worse (Pitman gone, Pierce hurt, QB coming off an Achilles).

justin jefferson.note: Talent is fine, the QB is the risk. Last year proved he is not QB-proof, and FSE does not trust Kyler Murray — Brissett produced more for McBride, Harrison and Wilson than Murray did.

drake london.note: WR7 in points per game last season at age 25 with no repeatable injury pattern; he was playing out of his mind before the games he left early. Either Atlanta QB is good enough to feed him.

brock bowers.note: Cleanest TE projection in football, could outscore the WRs going near him. Risks are all situational — Jeanty banged up, Kubiak coming in, possible QB turmoil capping pass volume.

derrick henry.note: No such thing as a safe 33-year-old RB. Note the shape of last year — he was not smashing his per-game numbers until huge Weeks 16-17; average games there and he finishes around RB12. Declan Doyle addition is a plus.

trey mcbride.note: Safe. He produced with this same offense and QB last year, and the situation improved (healthy Marvin Harrison, revamped RB room incl. the No. 3 overall pick).

george pickens.note: Safe but capped. He made his money in Weeks 4-9 while CeeDee Lamb was out; without a Lamb injury he probably has no WR6 ceiling. Dallas volume and TD upside keep the floor high.

breece hall.note: Groin strain, expected healthy for Week 1. He was RB6 in points per game the last time the Jets offense was even half-decent, one year off an ACL, and 70+ catches gives him a floor. Question is Jets quality and true health.

tee higgins.note: Safe on touchdowns: 11 and 10 receiving TDs the last two years is repeatable with Burrow and Cincinnati's pass volume, even though Chase out-targets him by a mile.

garrett wilson.note: One of FSE's favorite picks. Good headspace under Frank Reich with Geno Smith, and he averaged 19 PPG in his first five games last year with Justin Fields throwing before the injury.

jaylen waddle.note: Denver's clear WR1 on an offense that threw 612 times despite an elite defense, and FSE rates him well above Courtland Sutton at this stage. He calls ESPN's fifth-round price a big value gap.

tetairoa mcmillan.note: Bad offense, shaky QB, and Carolina is one of the slowest, lowest-pass-volume teams. Jaylen Coker's return from injury visibly cut his target-earning from Week 13 (Rams game) onward.

jalen hurts.note: Safer than the skill players around him purely by being a QB with a long track record as a great producer.

caleb williams.note: Safe-ish for a QB — long-term optimism about the Ben Johnson offense in Chicago.

jadarian price.note: Ranked well ahead of his ESPN/Sleeper price. The bet is Seattle's first-round draft capital and good film; the risk is that he was a weak prospect stuck behind Jeremiyah Love in college with his own injury history.

marvin harrison jr..note: FSE will take the risk — he has cost much more than this before, and had he stayed healthy down the stretch he might have shown the late-season production Michael Wilson did.
